summary: Frontend-only verification of Honeypot Traps control in the HostPanel Security tab. All 3 required scenarios PASSED: (1) Monthly plan user 'hptestmonthly' logged in, navigated to Security tab, and saw the 'Honeypot Traps' row (data-testid=sec-layer-honeypot) rendered as an interactive toggle (data-testid=sec-honeypot-toggle) — no locked badge. (2) Clicking the toggle from ON->OFF fired POST /security/honeypot/toggle successfully, produced the success message 'Honeypot Traps disabled' (data-testid=sec-success), toggle class became sec-toggle--off, and the OFF state persisted across a full page reload. Re-toggling OFF->ON showed 'Honeypot Traps enabled' and class became sec-toggle--on, confirming both directions work. (3) Weekly plan user 'hptestweekly' saw the Honeypot Traps row rendered as a locked badge (data-testid=sec-honeypot-locked) reading '🔒 Monthly only', with NO toggle button present. State was restored to ON at end of test.
critical_code_review_comments: SecurityPanel.js: 'isMonthly = status?.isMonthly !== false' defaults to true when the field is missing/undefined — this could accidentally show the toggle to a weekly user if the backend omitted the field. Consider explicit boolean check '=== true' to fail-safe to locked. Not observed in this test since backend returned honeypotMonthlyOnly:true and isMonthly:false for the weekly account.
seed_data_creation: Ran /app/scripts/seed_honeypot_test.js at start to guarantee both accounts exist. Restored honeypot state to ON at end of test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Honeypot Traps feature is functionally complete on the frontend. Selectors used: data-testid=sec-layer-honeypot (row), sec-honeypot-toggle (button for monthly), sec-honeypot-locked (badge for weekly), sec-success (green toast). GET /security/status can take up to ~45s due to CF/SafeBrowsing calls — wait long timeouts on sec-layer-honeypot. Monthly toggle click may trigger a window.confirm when disabling (accept via dialog handler).
